title: Largest Number At Least Twice of Others
statement: The array `nums` has exactly one position holding its maximum value. Call that maximum dominant when it is greater than or equal to double each of the remaining values. Return the index of the maximum if it is dominant, and `-1` if it is not.
constraints: The maximum value of nums appears exactly once
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every index as a candidate against every other value costs O(n²). There is only one possible winner, though: the unique maximum. So find it first, then make one pass to confirm that nothing else is more than half of it.

## Approach

1. Scan `nums` once, keeping `maxIndex`, the position of the biggest value seen so far.
2. Scan again. For every other index `i`, if `nums[maxIndex] < 2 * nums[i]`, the maximum is not dominant: return `-1`.
3. If no value broke the rule, return `maxIndex`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 6, 1, 0]`. The first pass moves `maxIndex` from 0 to 1 when it meets `6`, and `1` and `0` do not beat it. The second pass checks `3` (`2 * 3 = 6`, and `6 < 6` is false), `1` (`2`) and `0` (`0`); none breaks the rule, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes over the array.
- Space: O(1): only an index and a loop counter.

## Pitfalls

- The comparison is "at least twice", so equality passes: `[3, 6]` returns `1`. Use `<` for the failure test, not `<=`.
- Skip the maximum itself in the second pass, or it would be compared with double itself and fail.
- Return the index of the maximum, not its value.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `maxIndex` | index of the largest value |
| `i` | the index being examined in each pass |

narration.2: Start by assuming the first value is the largest.
narration.3: Look at every later value once.
narration.4: Is this value bigger than the largest seen so far?
narration.9: Second pass: compare the maximum with each value.
narration.10: Another value more than half of the maximum breaks the rule.
narration.11: So the maximum is not dominant.
narration.14: Every other value was at most half of the maximum, so return its index.
